page: Amazon Web Services g7e.8xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores) operating at 2.4 GHz, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For graphics and parallel computing workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace RTX Pro 6000 GPU with 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the instance's capabilities across compute, memory, and specialized AI workloads. It achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference, processing 11350.44 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 1314.55 tokens per second on a large 70B model. Text generation speeds reach 221.14 tokens per second for a 7B model and 31.02 tokens per second for a 70B model, placing it in the top tier for LLM tasks. Geekbench single-core and image processing benchmarks also rank in the top tier, while multi-core performance, text processing, and bzip3 decompression are rated as strong.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g7e.8xlarge offers a high-density resource profile by bundling a professional-grade GPU with a large 96 GB VRAM buffer, high-speed DDR5 memory, and local NVMe storage. This dense integration reduces the need for external network-attached storage or multi-node configurations for large models. However, a potential tradeoff is the moderate CPU clock speed of 2.4 GHz, which delivers average single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance compared to pure compute-optimized instances.

This instance is highly suited for large language model (LLM) inference, deep learning, and advanced image processing tasks. The combination of 96 GB of GPU VRAM, 256 GB of system memory, and 100 Gbps network bandwidth also makes it appropriate for graphics-intensive rendering, data science pipelines, and high-throughput database operations.
